?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc-Lko:13718
Court No. - 15
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 3056 of 2023
Applicant :- Sunil Kumar Singh
Opposite Party :- Central Bureau Of Investigation Anti Curruption Branch Lko.

Counsel for Applicant :- Himanshu Hemant Gupta
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Anurag Kumar Singh
Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as Shri Anurag Kumar Singh, learned counse for C.B.I. and perused the record.
2.

The present application has been moved by the accused-applicant- Sunil Kumar Singh in Case No.
RC0062011A0007 of 2011, under Sections-120B, 420, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C. and Section 13(2) read with Section 13(1)(d) of P.C. Act, 1988, Police Station- SPE/ACB, District- Lucknow, with the prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail as he is apprehending arrest in the above-mentioned case.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant while pressing the anticipatory bail application submits that it is a case of false allegation.

Allegations against the applicant are to the tune that the company namely M/s Shree Ram Fuels Pvt. Ltd. in connivance with the officer/official of District Industries Center and of Northern Coalfields, District- Singrauli (M.P.) had executed a coal supply agreement for the purpose of processing and manufacturing special smokeless coal, the purchaser company sold the coal in open market, at premium, in violation of the terms of the written agreement and the allegations against the applicant's company is that the said company had purchased the same.

sentences.text:
It is further submitted by learned counsel for the applicant while drawing the attention of this Court towards Para 11 of the anticipatory bail application submits that written contract was entered into between the parties was an exhaustive document covering all the eventualities including the diversion of coal by the signatory of the contract and the penalty for diversion of coal in open market was also provided and provisions for forfeiture of security money and termination of the contract was also provided and therefore, the same may not generate any criminal consequence.
6.

It is also submitted that the applicant has also given bank guarantee to the tune of Rs.
38.96.923/- and the same has been forfeited in consequence of the said alleged breach of agreement and by instituting the instant case, the applicant has been subjected to double jeopardy.
7. It is also submitted that the applicant has cooperated throughout the investigation and the charge-sheet has also been submitted without arresting him.

8. It is also submitted that two co-accused persons namely Ramji Singh and Yogendra Nath Pandey who are government servants have been granted anticipatory bail in ABAIL No. 10848 of 2021,
ABAIL No. 12682 of 2021, ABAIL No. 12073 of 2021 and ABAIL No. 11618 of 2021 vide orders dated 16.11.2021, 02.11.2021, 26.10.2021 and 18.10.2021, respectively and the role of the instant applicant is on better footing than them.

9. It is also submitted that the applicant was also granted interim protection by this Court vide order dated 22.12.2023 under some conditions and he has remained abide by those conditions and has not violated any of the conditions under which his liberty was protected and it is undertaken that the applicant shall remain present before the trial Court/special Court as and when his presence would be required and he will not seek any adjournment when the prosecution witness would be examined.

10. It is also submitted that before involvement of the applicant in the instant case, he was not having any criminal antecedent and on the basis of his alleged involvement in the instant case, a case has been registered by the E.D.
11.

Shri Anurag Kumar Singh, learned counse1. l for C.B.I. on the other hand has vehemently opposed the anticipatory bail of the applicant but he could not dispute that the applicant was not arrested during the course of the investigation and also that the applicant has cooperated a throughout the investigation.

12. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it appears to be an admitted scenario that after lodging of the FIR, the applicant was not arrested by the Investigating Officer and the charge-sheet, in this case, has been submitted without making him arrest.

The applicant was also granted interim protection by this Court vide order dated 22.12.2023 and nothing has been brought before this Court which may suggest that the applicant has violated any of the conditions under which his liberty was protected.

Since, the applicant was not arrested during the course of the investigation, I do not find any reason as to why he be confined in the prison only for the purpose of disposal of his regular bail application.
More so, when he has not violated any of the conditions under which his liberty was protected vide order dated 22.12.2023.

Thus having regard to the reasons mentioned above and keeping in view the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre Vs State of Maharashtra and Ors.,
MANU/SC/1021/2010, Sushila Aggarwal and Ors. Vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and Ors.,
MANU/SC/0100/2020, Shri Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia and Ors. v. State of Punjab,
MANU/SC/0215/1980 : 1980 (2) SCC 565, and Nathu Singh Vs. State of U.P. and Others:(2021) 6 SCC 64, in the considered opinion of this court, having regard to the material/evidence available against the applicant, the order dated 22.12.2023 passed by this Court is made absolute.

and the anticipatory bail application, moved on behalf of the applicant - Sunil Kumar Singh is allowed with a direction that in the event of arrest of the applicant under any process of the trial Court or on his/her presence/surrender before the trial Court within 20 days from today i.e. till 05.03.2024 whichever is earlier, he/she shall be released forthwith on anticipatory bail on his/her furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, subject to the following conditions:-
(i). The applicant, if not arrested earlier, shall appear before the trial court within 20 days from today i.e. till 05.03.2024 and cooperate in the trial and shall not seek any adjournment when the prosecution witness would be in attendance.

(ii). In case of further investigation or re-investigation the applicant shall cooperate in the investigation and make himself/herself available as and when required by the Investigating officer of the case, even for the recovery of any fact.
(iii).
The applicant shall not make any attempt to influence the prosecution witnesses and will also not commit any crime during his/her release on anticipatory bail.

(iv). The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he/she shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence and specially when the prosecution witnesses are present in court.

(v). The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
14.

If in the opinion of the trial court default of any of the condition placed above is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and shall proceed against him/her in accordance with law.
15. It is clarified that all the observations contained in this order are only for disposal of this anticipatory bail application and shall not affect the trial proceedings in any manner.
